description: Draws a random voltage on each clock from a seedable random source, with three outputs carrying three different distributions

params.text: While on, the values are drawn over -5V to 5V; while off, over 0-10V
Sets how many uniform draws each value is made from, 1 to 20; at 1 every output carries a plain uniform distribution
Sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16

inputs.text: The clock that draws a new set of values
A trigger here reseeds the random source from the voltage at Seed and draws a value at once, so the same run of values is drawn again
Sets the seed, 0-10V across the seed range, read only at the instant a trigger arrives at Rst; at 0V, and with nothing patched, the seed is taken from the computer's clock instead
Sets the number of draws by voltage in place of the Sth knob, 0-10V mapped onto 1 to 20, one channel per output channel

outputs.text: The smallest of the draws, which crowds the values towards the bottom of the range as Sth is raised
A Weibull distribution with its density set by Sth
The average of the draws, which crowds the values towards the middle of the range as Sth is raised and approaches a normal distribution

notes: with nothing patched into Clk a new value is drawn every sample, giving noise at audio rate, and the values are then drawn over -5V to 5V whatever the BiP button is set to
menu: Round Seed — cuts the voltage at Seed to four decimal places before it is turned into a seed, so a seed set by hand can be hit again

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads half the Sth knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
